strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations where each iteration computes scaling factors from the previous result, applies them, and reduces. This is the baseline approach with 8 all-reduce dispatches. Trades simplicity and correctness for maximum latency due to sequential dependencies.

strategies.name: Fused buffer all-reduce with vectorized scaling
strategies.desc: Concatenates all 8 iterations' buffers into a single payload and dispatches one large all-reduce per iteration, amortizing launch overhead. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but with better memory locality and potential for vectorized local operations on the combined buffer. Trades memory footprint for reduced per-dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Pipelined reduce-scatter then all-gather
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing overlap of computation (mean-square calculation, scaling) during the scatter phase with communication in subsequent stages. Results in 16 collective dispatches (2 per iteration) but enables pipeline parallelism between computation and communication phases.

strategies.name: Block-parallel independent initialization then synchronized refinement
strategies.desc: Performs initial all-reduce once, then computes all 8 blocks' scaling factors in parallel across the iteration dependency chain by maintaining separate buffers per block. Uses 1 initial + 7 incremental all-reduces with larger payloads. Trades memory (8x block buffers) for potential parallelism in local computation.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction for large world
strategies.desc:
Exploits world_size=224 by organizing into node-local groups, performing intra-node reductions first, then inter-node reductions with a designated rank per node. Approximately 8×2=16 dispatches (intra+inter per iteration) but each operates on smaller effective world sizes. Trades dispatch count for reduced per-dispatch latency via hierarchical topology.
